## Your destination

By the end, you should be able to identify the three PLINK input files, run a
command from R, explain missingness and allele-frequency filters, and account for
the samples and variants remaining after each step.

**Core walkthrough:** complete sections 1–7 in order. **Try it yourself:** keep a
short record of your predictions and interpretations. **Going further:** optional
challenges at the end. You do not need to finish them to start lesson 2.

## Start with a clean session

Open `GWAS_training_session.Rproj`, then this notebook. Use **Session → Restart R**.
Run one chunk at a time with the green arrow, or Ctrl+Shift+Enter on Windows/Linux
and Cmd+Shift+Enter on macOS. Do not use Run All before reading the lesson.

```{r qc-setup}
root <- if (file.exists("R/course.R")) "." else ".."
source(file.path(root, "R", "course.R"))
cfg <- course_config(root)
print(check_bed(cfg$input))
```

**Check your result:** the message identifies `demo` or `course`. Demo means
simulated practice data, not the original study. A missing BED message means you
must complete [setup](../docs/setup.md) before continuing.

### Which window am I using?

| Window | What you type there | Example |
|---|---|---|
| R console | R expressions; the prompt is usually `>` | `2 + 2` |
| Terminal | Operating-system commands | `plink2 --version` |
| Notebook editor | Saved instructions and R chunks | The chunks on this page |

Our notebook calls PLINK from R. A printed PLINK command explains what is being
executed; you do not have to paste it into the R console.

## Meet the files and identifiers

**The question:** how do we connect genotypes to the right person and variant?

| File | One record represents | Open as ordinary text? |
|---|---|---|
| `.bed` | Packed genotype calls, interpreted with BIM and FAM | No |
| `.bim` | A variant: chromosome, ID, genetic distance, position, two alleles | Yes |
| `.fam` | A sample: FID, IID, parental IDs, sex code, phenotype | Yes |

```{r qc-inspect-files}
fam <- read_fam(cfg$input)
bim <- read_ws(paste0(cfg$input, ".bim"), header = FALSE)
head(fam)
head(bim)
metadata <- prepare_metadata(cfg)
table(metadata$Disease, useNA = "ifany")
```

**Check your result:** one FAM row per sample and six BIM columns. Disease uses
`1 = control`, `2 = case`, missing = unavailable. FID and IID stay as text so that
leading zeros are preserved. Matching both identifiers prevents accidental joins
between different people. Extra metadata records are not added to the genotype set.

**Try it yourself — Q1:** which file would you inspect for a variant's physical
position? Which two columns would you use to match a covariate record to a sample?

## Establish the starting dataset

**Before you run:** inputs are read without being overwritten. Outputs go into
`results/demo/` or `results/course/`. Each PLINK command creates a log, a captured
console file and a command record.

```{r qc-prepare}
start <- file.path(cfg$qc, "01_autosomes")
run_plink(cfg, c("--bfile", cfg$input, "--autosome",
                "--update-sex", file.path(cfg$out, "sex.tsv"),
                "--pheno", file.path(cfg$out, "phenotype.tsv"), "--pheno-name", "Disease",
                "--make-bed", "--out", start), paste0(start, c(".bed", ".bim", ".fam")))
record_counts(cfg, start, "01_autosomes")
run_plink(cfg, c("--bfile", start, "--missing", "--out", file.path(cfg$qc, "before")),
          file.path(cfg$qc, c("before.smiss", "before.vmiss")))
```

`--bfile` names the input prefix, `--autosome` selects chromosomes 1–22,
`--make-bed` writes a new binary set, and `--out` names the output prefix.
This core exercise concerns autosomes. Sex-chromosome QC requires additional
genome-build and pseudo-autosomal-region checks; see the optional section below.

## Inspect missingness before filtering

**The question:** are missing calls concentrated in particular samples or variants?

```{r qc-missingness, fig.alt="Two histograms show the distributions of sample and variant missing-call fractions before filtering."}
smiss <- read_ws(file.path(cfg$qc, "before.smiss"))
vmiss <- read_ws(file.path(cfg$qc, "before.vmiss"))
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
hist(as.numeric(smiss$F_MISS), breaks = 30, main = "Sample missingness", xlab = "Missing-call fraction")
abline(v = cfg$mind, col = "#B45309", lty = 2)
hist(as.numeric(vmiss$F_MISS), breaks = 30, main = "Variant missingness", xlab = "Missing-call fraction")
abline(v = cfg$geno, col = "#B45309", lty = 2)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

**Try it yourself — Q2:** a sample has 9% missing calls and a variant has 6%.
With `--mind 0.10` and `--geno 0.05`, which passes its own missingness criterion?
Explain what denominator each percentage uses.

## Apply and audit the filters

Thresholds below are teaching choices, not a universal GWAS protocol. We filter
poorly called variants, then poorly called samples, then low-frequency variants.
Changing the order can change the retained set because the denominators change.

```{r qc-filters}
geno <- file.path(cfg$qc, "02_geno")
run_plink(cfg, c("--bfile", start, "--geno", cfg$geno, "--make-bed", "--out", geno))
record_counts(cfg, geno, "02_geno")
mind <- file.path(cfg$qc, "03_mind")
run_plink(cfg, c("--bfile", geno, "--mind", cfg$mind, "--make-bed", "--out", mind))
record_counts(cfg, mind, "03_mind")
maf <- file.path(cfg$qc, "04_maf")
run_plink(cfg, c("--bfile", mind, "--maf", cfg$maf, "--make-bed", "--out", maf))
record_counts(cfg, maf, "04_maf")
```

**Check your result:** read `sample_variant_counts.tsv`. A zero change can be a
valid result; do not invent an expected number of exclusions. MAF is an allele
frequency, not the frequency of people carrying an allele.

## Heterozygosity and relatedness

**The question:** do unusual genotype patterns or close relatives require review?
First select a set of common, approximately independent variants.

```{r qc-pruning-and-het}
prune <- file.path(cfg$qc, "prune")
run_plink(cfg, c("--bfile", maf, "--maf", "0.05", "--indep-pairwise", "200", "50", "0.2",
                "--out", prune), paste0(prune, ".prune.in"))
run_plink(cfg, c("--bfile", maf, "--extract", paste0(prune, ".prune.in"),
                "--het", "--out", file.path(cfg$qc, "heterozygosity")),
          file.path(cfg$qc, "heterozygosity.het"))
het <- read_ws(file.path(cfg$qc, "heterozygosity.het"))
summary(as.numeric(het$F))
```

```{r qc-het-plot, fig.alt="Histogram of sample inbreeding-coefficient estimates used to review unusual heterozygosity."}
hist(as.numeric(het$F), breaks = 30, main = "Review heterozygosity", xlab = "F coefficient")
```

An unusual F value is a reason to investigate. It can reflect ancestry,
inbreeding, contamination or another technical problem. We do not automatically
remove every sample beyond a pooled mean ±3 SD.

```{r qc-relatedness}
king <- file.path(cfg$qc, "relatedness")
run_plink(cfg, c("--bfile", maf, "--extract", paste0(prune, ".prune.in"),
                "--king-cutoff", cfg$kinship, "--out", king), paste0(king, ".king.cutoff.in.id"))
final <- file.path(cfg$qc, "qc_final")
# Apply the sample list to ALL QC-passing variants, not just the pruned subset.
run_plink(cfg, c("--bfile", maf, "--keep", paste0(king, ".king.cutoff.in.id"),
                "--make-bed", "--out", final))
record_counts(cfg, final, "05_unrelated")
read.delim(file.path(cfg$qc, "sample_variant_counts.tsv"))
```

KING kinship is approximately 0.5 for duplicate samples, 0.25 for first-degree
relatives and 0.125 for second-degree relatives. The course cutoff, 0.0884,
screens close relationships through roughly the second degree. Estimates vary;
this is not the same quantity as PLINK 1.9's PI_HAT. In research, which relative
to retain also depends on call quality and study design.

## Finish and restart later

Your checkpoint is the **three-file set** `01_qc/qc_final.bed/.bim/.fam` plus
`metadata.tsv` and the count table. Lesson 2 reads files from disk; it does not
depend on this R environment. See [recovery](../docs/troubleshooting.md#rejoining-the-class).

**Exit check — Q3:** sample counts decrease at the relatedness step, but almost all
variants remain. Explain why this is different from using the pruned variants as
the final association dataset. Name one log you would inspect before accepting it.

### Going further

- Predict the effect of reducing `--mind` from 0.10 to 0.05. Try a separate output
  prefix and compare counts without overwriting the core workflow.
- For HWE, distinguish a diagnostic in controls from a filter applied to the
  complete study. You will inspect this after the PCA in lesson 2.
- For sex consistency, use the original unfiltered input with X/Y markers only
  after confirming the genome build and splitting PAR correctly. Read the
  [PLINK sex-check documentation](https://www.cog-genomics.org/plink/2.0/basic_stats#check_sex).
  A discrepancy needs review, not an automatic change of recorded information.
